specName: Curated Skills Library — Three-Source Library, Match & Inject, Model Suggestions, Run View Skills Tab
title: rorca-curated-skills-library
_notes:
Builds on existing SkillRegistry (SK-001), suggestedSkills in spec JSON (SK-002), loadMatchedSkills in execution-engine (SK-003), and active_skills column in story_results. The skills infrastructure is ~70% built — this spec fills the remaining UX gaps: three-source skills library (skills.sh / GitHub repos / custom upload), explicit Match & Inject action, model suggestion per story, Skills tab in Run View, and effectiveness analytics. Source repo for skills: https://github.com/wojons/skills.

userStories.title: GitHub Repository Skill Browser API
userStories.description: Add two new backend API endpoints that let users browse and install skills directly from any GitHub repository (e.g., wojons/skills, sysgazer/skills, vercel-labs/agent-skills) without going through skills.sh search. The browse endpoint lists all SKILL.md files in a repo tree. The install endpoint fetches a specific SKILL.md by path and installs it using the existing SkillRegistry.install() flow with dual-save to .rorca/skills/ and .claude/skills/.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/skills/browse-github endpoint added to backend/src/routes/skills.ts
Request body: { repoUrl: string } where repoUrl is a GitHub URL like 'https://github.com/wojons/skills' or shorthand 'wojons/skills'

Parses owner/repo from URL — strips 'https://github.com/', '.git' suffix, '/tree/main' suffix, trailing slashes. Examples: 'https://github.com/wojons/skills/tree/main' -> owner='wojons', repo='skills'. 'wojons/skills' -> same.
Calls GitHub Tree API: GET https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/HEAD?recursive=1
Filters response for files matching glob pattern '*/SKILL.md' at any depth (e.g., skills/react/SKILL.md, react/SKILL.md)

For each SKILL.md found, fetches the raw content from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/{owner}/{repo}/main/{path} to parse YAML frontmatter for 'name' and 'description' fields. If main branch 404s, tries 'master' branch.
Response shape: { repo: string, branch: string, skills: Array<{ name: string, description: string, path: string, installed: boolean }> }

The 'installed' boolean is computed by checking if name.toLowerCase() exists in the current SkillRegistry (call discover() with workspace path resolved from ?workspaceId query param or first registered workspace)
Timeout: 15 seconds for GitHub API calls. Returns 502 with { error: 'GitHub API unavailable' } on timeout
Rate limiting: if GitHub returns 403, return 429 with { error: 'GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Try again later or add a GitHub token in Settings.' }
Returns 400 with { error: 'Invalid repository URL' } if repoUrl cannot be parsed to owner/repo
Returns 404 with { error: 'Repository not found' } if GitHub returns 404 on tree API
Has @swagger JSDoc annotation with full request/response schema
POST /api/skills/install-from-github endpoint added to backend/src/routes/skills.ts
Request body: { repoUrl: string, skillPath: string, workspaceId?: string } where skillPath is the path within the repo (e.g., 'skills/react/SKILL.md')
Fetches raw content from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/{owner}/{repo}/main/{skillPath}. If main 404s, tries master.
Parses YAML frontmatter for 'name' and 'description'. If no frontmatter, derives name from directory name (e.g., 'skills/react/SKILL.md' -> 'react')
Resolves workspace path using same resolveWorkspacePath() helper pattern already in skills.ts install-from-sh endpoint
Creates .rorca/skills/ and .claude/skills/ directories if they don't exist (fs.mkdirSync recursive:true)
Writes content to BOTH .rorca/skills/{name}.md AND .claude/skills/{name}.md (same dual-save pattern as install-from-sh)
Calls registry.install(name, content, 'github:{owner}/{repo}') to persist in DB
Response: { name, description, source, filePath } with status 201
Returns 404 if skill file not found at path in either main or master branch
Returns 400 if repoUrl or skillPath missing from request body
Has @swagger JSDoc annotation

userStories.title: Explicit Match & Inject Skills API
userStories.description: Add a new API endpoint that explicitly triggers LLM-driven skill matching for an existing spec. Takes an approved or pending spec, sends the curated skill catalog + spec stories + MEMORY.md + AGENTS.md to the LLM, receives per-story skill assignments with relevance scores and reasoning, and WRITES the suggestedSkills arrays directly back to the spec JSON file. This is the 'inject' part — once written, the execution engine's existing loadMatchedSkills() will automatically pick them up during pipeline runs. The endpoint also creates a spec version for audit trail.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/specs/:id/match-skills endpoint added to backend/src/routes/specs.ts
Request body: { workspaceId: string }
Reads the spec JSON file from either forge/specs/pending/{id}.json or forge/specs/approved/{id}.json (tries approved first, then pending — same resolution pattern as existing spec routes)
Calls buildCatalogContext(workspacePath) (already at specs.ts:175) to get installed skill catalog, MEMORY.md, and AGENTS.md
If skill catalog is empty (no installed skills), returns 422 with { error: 'No skills installed. Install skills from the Marketplace before matching.' }

Constructs LLM prompt with: (1) system message explaining the task, (2) the compact skill catalog (one line per skill: 'name: description'), (3) MEMORY.md content (truncated to 2000 chars if longer), (4) AGENTS.md content (truncated to 2000 chars if longer), (5) all story IDs + titles + descriptions as a numbered list

System message instructs: 'You are a skill-matching agent. For each story, select the most relevant skills from the installed catalog. Use MEMORY.md entries as the strongest signal — if MEMORY.md mentions past bugs with authentication, bias toward security-related skills for auth stories. Use AGENTS.md zone governance as secondary signal. Use story description text as tertiary signal.'

Prompt instructs LLM to output valid JSON: { matches: [{ storyId: 'US-001', suggestedSkills: [{ name: 'react', relevance: 8, reason: 'Story involves React component creation — MEMORY.md notes React 18 conventions are critical' }] }] }

Relevance scoring instructions in prompt: '10 = this skill is essential for the story, 7-9 = highly relevant, 4-6 = moderately helpful, 1-3 = tangentially related. Only include skills with relevance >= 4. If no skills apply to a story, return empty suggestedSkills array.'
Uses chatComplete() from llm-client.ts with the workspace's preferred model (same resolution chain as spec generation: explicit model param -> workspace L3 preferred_model -> DEFAULT_MODEL)
Parses LLM JSON response. Validates skill names against skillNames set from buildCatalogContext() using validateSuggestedSkills() (already at specs.ts:202). Strips unknown names.

Writes updated suggestedSkills arrays back to each story in the spec JSON file. Preserves ALL other fields (title, description, acceptanceCriteria, dependsOn, etc.) — only suggestedSkills is modified. Uses JSON.stringify with 2-space indent.
Creates a spec version entry in spec_versions table with version_type = 'skill_match' for audit trail (same INSERT pattern as existing spec version creation in specs.ts)
Emits WAL event: { event_type: 'skill_matched', payload: JSON.stringify({ spec_id: id, workspace_id: workspaceId, matched_count: totalSkillsMatched, stories_affected: storiesWithSkills.length }) }
Response: { matched: number, stories: Array<{ storyId: string, skills: Array<{ name: string, relevance: number, reason: string }> }> } with status 200
Returns 404 if spec file not found in either pending or approved directory
Returns 400 if workspaceId missing from request body
Has @swagger JSDoc annotation with full request/response schema

userStories.title: Model Suggestion API
userStories.description: Add a new API endpoint that uses the LLM to suggest the optimal execution model for each story in a spec, based on story complexity, description content, dependsOn depth, and the workspace's available models. Returns SUGGESTIONS only — does not auto-apply. The user reviews and accepts/denies per story. When accepted, the 'model' field is written to the story in the spec JSON.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/specs/:id/suggest-models endpoint added to backend/src/routes/specs.ts
Request body: { workspaceId: string, availableModels?: string[] }
If availableModels not provided, uses SUPPORTED_MODELS list from llm-client.ts as the default set
Reads the spec JSON file (same resolution as SL-002: approved first, then pending)

Constructs LLM prompt with: (1) list of available models with their characteristics (e.g., 'claude-haiku-4-5-20251001: fast, cheap, good for simple CRUD and config changes' / 'claude-sonnet-4-6: balanced, good for standard features' / 'claude-opus-4-6: most capable, best for architecture, security, complex logic'), (2) all story IDs + titles + descriptions + acceptanceCriteria count + dependsOn depth + complexity field (if set)

System message: 'You are a model-routing advisor. For each story, suggest the most cost-effective model that can reliably complete the task. Consider: stories with many acceptance criteria or complex dependencies need stronger models. Simple UI tweaks, copy changes, and config updates can use the cheapest model. Security-sensitive, architecture, and payment stories should always use the strongest available model.'
Output format: { suggestions: [{ storyId: 'US-001', suggestedModel: 'claude-sonnet-4-6', reason: 'Standard feature with 5 acceptance criteria — Sonnet is sufficient', confidence: 0.85 }] }
confidence field is 0.0-1.0 indicating how confident the LLM is in the suggestion. Low confidence (< 0.6) means the user should pay extra attention.
Does NOT write to the spec JSON file — returns suggestions only
Response: { suggestions: Array<{ storyId: string, currentModel: string | null, suggestedModel: string, reason: string, confidence: number }> } with status 200
currentModel is read from the story's existing 'model' field (null if not set)
Returns 404 if spec not found, 400 if workspaceId missing
Has @swagger JSDoc annotation

userStories.title: Skills Usage Per-Run API Endpoint
userStories.description: Add a new API endpoint GET /api/pipeline/runs/:runId/skills that returns per-story skill usage data for a specific pipeline run. Aggregates data from the active_skills column in story_results and enriches it with skill metadata from the spec JSON's suggestedSkills (for relevance scores and reasons) and the installed_skills table (for descriptions). Also computes a run-level summary with skill frequency and pass-rate correlation.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/pipeline/runs/:runId/skills endpoint added to backend/src/routes/pipeline.ts
Query: SELECT story_id, status, active_skills, model_used FROM story_results WHERE run_id = ? ORDER BY id ASC
For each story with non-null active_skills (JSON array string), parses the array and resolves skill metadata
Also reads the spec JSON file (via pipeline_runs.spec_path joined with workspaces.path) to get suggestedSkills per story — this provides 'relevance' and 'reason' fields not stored in story_results
Skill descriptions resolved from installed_skills table by name. If skill uninstalled since run, description is null.

Response shape: { runId: number, perStory: Array<{ storyId: string, storyTitle: string, storyStatus: string, skills: Array<{ name: string, relevance: number | null, reason: string | null, description: string | null, category: string | null }> }>, summary: { totalSkillInjections: number, uniqueSkills: string[], skillFrequency: Array<{ name: string, count: number, passRate: number, category: string | null }>, storiesWithSkills: number, storiesWithoutSkills: number } }
storyTitle is resolved from spec JSON's userStories array by matching storyId
skillFrequency[].passRate = (stories where skill active AND status='pass') / (stories where skill active). Returns 0.0 if denominator is 0.
summary.uniqueSkills sorted by frequency descending (most used first)
summary.skillFrequency sorted by count descending
Stories with null or empty active_skills have skills: [] in response
If spec JSON is missing/unreadable, relevance and reason default to null (names and descriptions still available)
Returns 400 for non-numeric runId, 404 for unknown run (no row in pipeline_runs)
Has @swagger JSDoc annotation with full response schema

userStories.title: Skill Curation Bulk Operations
userStories.description: Add bulk operation endpoints for managing the curated skills collection. Users need to install multiple skills at once (e.g., all from a GitHub repo browse), remove multiple skills, and export their curated list as a shareable JSON manifest that can be re-imported in another workspace.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/skills/bulk-install endpoint added to backend/src/routes/skills.ts
Request body: { skills: Array<{ name: string, source: 'sh' | 'github', repoUrl?: string, skillPath?: string, content?: string }>, workspaceId?: string }

Processes skills sequentially (not parallel — avoids GitHub rate limiting). For source='sh', calls same fetchSkillFromRegistry() logic as install-from-sh. For source='github', fetches from raw.githubusercontent.com using repoUrl+skillPath (same as SL-001 install-from-github). For items with content provided directly, installs from the raw markdown content.
Each skill goes through the full install pipeline: parse frontmatter, dual-save to .rorca/skills/ + .claude/skills/, register in DB via SkillRegistry.install()
Response: { installed: number, failed: Array<{ name: string, error: string }>, total: number } with status 200
Failed items do not abort the batch — processing continues. Error message per failed item describes what went wrong (404, parse error, etc.)
POST /api/skills/bulk-remove endpoint added to backend/src/routes/skills.ts
Request body: { names: string[], workspaceId?: string }
For each name: calls registry.remove(name), deletes .rorca/skills/{name}.md and .claude/skills/{name}.md from filesystem (fs.unlinkSync wrapped in try/catch — missing files are not errors)
Response: { removed: number, notFound: string[] } with status 200
GET /api/skills/export endpoint added to backend/src/routes/skills.ts
Query param: workspaceId (optional)
Returns a JSON manifest: { skills: Array<{ name: string, description: string, source: string, category: string | null }>, exportedAt: string, workspacePath: string | null }
This manifest can be saved and used to re-install the same skill set (via bulk-install with source='sh' or by fetching from original sources)
All three endpoints have @swagger JSDoc annotations

userStories.title: Skill Category Tags
userStories.description: Add optional 'category' and 'tags' fields to skill metadata (YAML frontmatter) and the installed_skills table. This enables filtering skills by category (Frontend, Backend, Testing, DevOps, Security, Database, Workflow, Adversarial) in both the Marketplace and the Skills tab. Skills without explicit categories are auto-categorized using keyword matching on the skill name and description.
acceptanceCriteria: Add 'category TEXT' and 'tags TEXT' columns to installed_skills table via pragma table_info check in backend/src/db/index.ts (same pattern as other column additions — NOT a migration file). 'tags' stores a JSON array string.
SkillRegistry Skill interface in skill-registry.ts updated: metadata gains optional 'category: string' and 'tags: string[]' fields
SkillRegistry.install() reads 'category' and 'tags' from YAML frontmatter if present. Tags can be comma-separated string or YAML array.
SkillRegistry.discover() populates category and tags from frontmatter for filesystem-discovered skills

If frontmatter has no 'category' field, auto-categorize using keyword matching: name/description containing 'react|vue|angular|css|tailwind|frontend|ui|component' -> 'Frontend', 'api|server|express|backend|database|sql|prisma' -> 'Backend', 'test|jest|vitest|playwright|cypress|qa' -> 'Testing', 'docker|deploy|ci|cd|devops|cloud|kubernetes' -> 'DevOps', 'security|auth|xss|csrf|injection|redteam|white-hat' -> 'Security', 'adversarial|assumption|devil|advocate|challenge' -> 'Adversarial', 'workflow|orchestrat|build|compile' -> 'Workflow'. Default category: 'General'.
GET /api/skills response includes 'category' and 'tags' fields per skill
DB INSERT/UPSERT for installed_skills includes category and tags columns
Existing skills in DB get category populated on next discover() call (category column defaults to NULL, auto-categorized on read)

userStories.title: Three-Tab Skills Library UI
userStories.description: Redesign the Skills section in MarketplaceView.tsx with three distinct sub-tabs for skill sources: (1) skills.sh — search the public marketplace, (2) GitHub Repos — browse and install from any GitHub repository, (3) Custom — paste markdown or upload a .md file. Above the tabs, show the curated/installed skills collection with category filters, bulk actions, and a prominent 'Match & Inject' button. This is the main skills curation interface.
acceptanceCriteria: In MarketplaceView.tsx, when the Skills tab is active, render a two-section layout: (1) top section = 'Your Skills Library' showing installed/curated skills, (2) bottom section = three sub-tabs for adding new skills

Top section — 'Your Skills Library' header with Wrench icon (already imported). Shows count: '{count} skills installed'. Below header: horizontal category filter pills — 'All', 'Frontend', 'Backend', 'Testing', 'DevOps', 'Security', 'Adversarial', 'Workflow', 'General'. Active pill has bg-accent/20 text-accent styling. Clicking a category filters the installed skills list below.

Installed skills displayed as a compact grid of cards (2 columns on desktop, 1 on mobile). Each card shows: skill name (font-semibold text-sm), description (text-xs text-muted, truncated 2 lines), category badge (text-[10px] font-mono, color matches category: Frontend=blue, Backend=green, Testing=amber, DevOps=purple, Security=red, Adversarial=pink, Workflow=cyan, General=gray), source badge (text-[10px] — 'skills.sh' / 'github:owner/repo' / 'custom'), and a remove button (Trash2 icon, size=12, text-red-400 on hover).

Action bar above the grid: 'Match & Inject' button (primary style: bg-accent text-white, Wrench icon) — this calls POST /api/specs/:id/match-skills (from SL-002). NOTE: MarketplaceView currently receives NO props and has no spec context (verified via deep-read). To enable this button, add an optional 'activeSpecId?: string' prop to MarketplaceView and thread it from the parent (SpecsPanel.tsx which renders <MarketplaceView /> at the marketplace tab). If activeSpecId is undefined, button is disabled with tooltip 'Generate a spec first to match skills'. 'Export' button (Download icon, secondary style). 'Remove All' button (Trash2 icon, destructive style — shows confirmation dialog before proceeding).
Bottom section — three sub-tabs rendered as pill buttons: 'skills.sh' (with Star icon), 'GitHub Repos' (with GitFork icon), 'Custom' (with FileText icon). Default active: skills.sh.

Sub-tab 1 — skills.sh: reuses existing search functionality (search input + results grid + install buttons). Same code currently in SkillsTab, extracted into this sub-tab. Search via POST /api/skills/search.

Sub-tab 2 — GitHub Repos: input field with placeholder 'Enter repo URL (e.g., wojons/skills)' and 'Browse' button. On submit, calls POST /api/skills/browse-github (SL-001). Results rendered as a list of skill cards with install buttons. 'Install All' button appears when 2+ uninstalled skills shown. Progress indicator during bulk install: '{current}/{total} installing...' using POST /api/skills/bulk-install (SL-005). After install, card status changes to 'Installed' with green Check icon without full refetch. Previously browsed repos remembered in component state (not persisted) — switching between sub-tabs preserves the browse results.

Sub-tab 3 — Custom: two options side by side. Option A: textarea (min-height 200px) with placeholder 'Paste SKILL.md content here...' and 'Install' button below. Textarea has monospace font (font-mono text-xs). On install, calls POST /api/skills/install with { name: parsed-from-frontmatter, content: textarea-value }. If no frontmatter name field, prompts user for a name via inline input that appears above textarea. Option B: file upload area with dashed border and 'Upload .md file' label. Accepts .md files only (accept='.md'). On file select, reads content via FileReader, previews in a read-only pre block, shows 'Install' button. File name (without .md extension) used as skill name if no frontmatter.

Empty state for installed skills: centered Wrench icon (opacity-30) with 'No skills installed yet' heading and 'Browse skills.sh, add from a GitHub repo, or paste your own' subtext. Three buttons pointing to each sub-tab.
Loading states: Loader2 spinner with descriptive text for each async operation (browsing, installing, searching)
Error states: inline error message in text-red-400 text-xs below the relevant action area. Errors clear on retry.

Toast notifications via useGlobalToast(): success on install ('Skill "{name}" installed'), success on bulk install ('{count} skills installed'), success on remove ('Skill "{name}" removed'), warning on no-frontmatter ('Skill installed without frontmatter — name derived from filename')

In the StoryReviewCard component (src/panels/SpecReviewPanel.tsx, line 265), within the expanded content section (line 397, inside the {expanded && ...} block), add a matched skills row BETWEEN the description block (line 400-403) and the per-story model override section (line 407-430). userStories.title: WAL Events for Skill Lifecycle
userStories.description: Emit WAL events when skills are installed, removed, or matched to specs. Creates an audit trail in the wal_events table and enables the activity feed and notification system to surface skill-related actions. All events go through the existing broadcastAll() from sse-hub.ts for real-time broadcast to connected clients.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/skills/install emits WAL event after successful install: { event_type: 'skill_installed', payload: JSON.stringify({ name, source, workspace_id }) }
POST /api/skills/install-from-sh emits WAL event: { event_type: 'skill_installed', payload: JSON.stringify({ name, source, skillId, workspace_id }) }
POST /api/skills/install-from-github (SL-001) emits WAL event: { event_type: 'skill_installed', payload: JSON.stringify({ name, source: 'github:{owner}/{repo}', repoUrl, workspace_id }) }
DELETE /api/skills/:name emits WAL event: { event_type: 'skill_removed', payload: JSON.stringify({ name, workspace_id }) }
POST /api/skills/bulk-install (SL-005) emits one skill_installed WAL event per successfully installed skill (not one event for the whole batch)
POST /api/skills/bulk-remove (SL-005) emits one skill_removed WAL event per successfully removed skill
POST /api/specs/:id/match-skills (SL-002) already emits skill_matched — verify it works and includes spec_id, workspace_id, matched_count, stories_affected in payload
PREREQUISITE — Add import to backend/src/routes/skills.ts: import { broadcastAll, type WalEvent } from '../lib/sse-hub' (verified pattern from backend/src/routes/worktrees.ts and budget.ts)

WAL events are written using the verified pattern from worktrees.ts: (1) const result = db.prepare('INSERT INTO wal_events (event_type, workspace_id, payload) VALUES (?, ?, ?)').run(eventType, workspaceId, JSON.stringify(payload)); (2) const walEvent = db.prepare('SELECT * FROM wal_events WHERE rowid = ?').get(result.lastInsertRowid) as WalEvent; (3) broadcastAll(walEvent);
All payloads include workspace_id when available (from request query/body or resolved from first registered workspace). If no workspace available, workspace_id is null.
WAL event_type values 'skill_installed', 'skill_removed', 'skill_matched' are documented in the CLAUDE.md WAL event types list

userStories.title: Skill Effectiveness Analytics API
userStories.description: Add a workspace-level analytics endpoint that aggregates skill effectiveness across all pipeline runs. Computes which skills correlate most with story success by analyzing the active_skills column in story_results across all runs for a workspace within a time range. Uses SQLite json_each() to explode the JSON array for aggregation.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/analytics/skills/effectiveness endpoint added to backend/src/routes/analytics.ts
Query parameters: workspaceId (required), since (optional ISO date string, defaults to 30 days ago: new Date(Date.now() - 30*24*60*60*1000).toISOString()), limit (optional number, default 20, max 50)

SQL query: SELECT sr.story_id, sr.status, sr.active_skills, sr.elapsed_seconds, pr.workspace_id FROM story_results sr JOIN pipeline_runs pr ON sr.run_id = pr.id WHERE pr.workspace_id = ? AND sr.started_at >= ? AND sr.active_skills IS NOT NULL

For each row, parse active_skills JSON array and aggregate per skill name. Can use SQLite json_each() if available: SELECT je.value AS skill_name, sr.status, sr.elapsed_seconds FROM story_results sr, json_each(sr.active_skills) je JOIN pipeline_runs pr ON sr.run_id = pr.id WHERE pr.workspace_id = ? AND sr.started_at >= ? AND sr.active_skills IS NOT NULL

Per skill: compute totalUses (count of stories), passCount (status='pass'), failCount (status='fail'), passRate (passCount/totalUses), avgElapsedSeconds (AVG(elapsed_seconds) for passed stories only — null if no passed stories), runsUsedIn (COUNT(DISTINCT sr.run_id))

Response shape: { skills: Array<{ name: string, totalUses: number, passCount: number, failCount: number, passRate: number, avgElapsedSeconds: number | null, runsUsedIn: number }>, period: { since: string, until: string }, totalRuns: number, totalStories: number }
skills array sorted by totalUses descending, limited to 'limit' parameter
totalRuns = COUNT(DISTINCT pr.id) for matching workspace+time. totalStories = COUNT(*) from story_results for matching runs+time.
Returns 400 if workspaceId missing. Returns empty skills: [] if no runs have skill data in the time range.
Has @swagger JSDoc annotation with full response schema
Note: better-sqlite3 bundles SQLite 3.40+ which supports json_each(). If json_each is unavailable (edge case), fall back to JavaScript-side JSON parsing of active_skills column.
